feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg, wheel_track 0.09 m, y 0.07 m, controller kp 2.5, kd 0.3) scored 400.0. Iteration 8 kept the same geometry and raised kp to 3.0 and kd to 0.45, scoring 610.7, with s-bend finishes rising from 2/20 to 15/20 and the oval at 20/20. That shows controller response, not geometry, was the remaining lever. Span (iteration 2), footprint (iteration 3), forward position (iteration 4), wheel_track (iterations 5 and 6) and mass (iteration 7) have all been tested, and none cleared the sharp tracks alone. Slalom has stayed at 0/20 with line-loss 1.9 to 1.95 through every geometry test, so it is probably a controller or line-loss-mode problem. Decision rules for the next race: (a) If s-bend line-loss is 1.0 or below and the oval holds at 16/20 or better, geometry is stable and the controller is the lever; hold geometry. (b) If slalom line-loss falls but the oval drops below about 14/20, the controller change is too strong and geometry should not change. (c) If slalom line-loss stays near 1.9 while s-bend holds, do not change geometry; the gap is the controller's response at direction changes, and the next iteration should test line_loss mode.
requested_changes: Hold wheel_track 0.09 m, span at plus or minus 0.03 m with 0.015 m spacing, sensor y 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m and mass 0.5 kg. Evidence: iteration 8 scored 610.7 on this geometry, and every geometry change from iteration 2 to 7 was flat or negative on the sharp tracks.

If the next race holds the oval at 16/20 or better but slalom stays at 1.9 line-loss, try mass 0.45 kg with the controller fixed. Evidence: mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg raised s-bend finishes from 0/20 to 2/20 (iteration 6 to 7), so a further small reduction is the only body lever with a trend, and it is not yet tested with the new gain.

If the oval falls below about 14/20 or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35 with low max_error, return mass to 0.7 kg. Evidence: at 0.7 kg the oval held oscillation at 0.30 (iteration 6), so a rise would indicate the lighter body is jittery under the stronger controller.
